precepts.text: Aaron and his sons waited on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
precepts.point: That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall wait on their priest’s office: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.” This is why Uzzah died when he took hold of the ark. The ark belonged to the priests’ office, and the stranger that came nigh it was to be put to death.

Every family of the priesthood had its own responsibility in the tabernacle service, and none could transgress against another’s charge. What the world later called unions came from that order.

The bounds at the mount are the same seriousness: “whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death”, “whether it be beast or man, it shall not live”.

precepts.text: Our Lord sprang out of Juda, of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood; no man of another tribe gave attendance at the altar.
precepts.point: Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

note.label: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest’s office, “and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.” Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

Paul shows the same law still standing in his day: “For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar. For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

Christ sprang out of Juda, and no man of that tribe gave attendance at the altar, because Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood for any tribe but Levi. Even the Lord’s own tribe was a stranger to the priest’s office under this law; only Aaron and his sons waited on it.

precepts.text: Uzzah took hold of the ark when his family was not chosen for that charge, and God smote him there for his error; he died by the ark of God.
precepts.point: Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.

note.label: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
The ending “ites” denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath, 8,600 males from a month old and upward, pitching on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was “the ark, and the table, and the candlestick, and the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary wherewith they minister.” Only they were responsible for the ark.

Anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, and generations later Uzzah showed it. “And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.”

Uzzah took hold of the ark when his family was not chosen for that charge, and God smote him on the spot. “And David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez–uzzah to this day.” The charge of the Kohathites was theirs alone.

precepts.text: The Levite has no part nor inheritance with thee; the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates shall come and eat and be satisfied.
precepts.point: The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

note.label: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at “five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary”, the shekel being twenty gerahs. Moses took that redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it “unto Aaron and to his sons.”

Why did the money go to Aaron and the priests? “And the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.” The Levite had no inheritance of his own, and he had to take care of the widows, the fatherless and the strangers. At the end of three years the tithe of the increase was laid up within the gates, “And the Levite, (because he hath no part nor inheritance with thee,) and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, which are within thy gates, shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied.”

The strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves, “that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hand which thou doest.”

precepts.text: The tribe of Levi is given to Aaron and his sons to wait on the priest's office; the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
precepts.point: They burn the daily burnt sacrifices morning and evening, set the shewbread in order, and keep the charge of the Most High that Jeroboam forsook.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Bring the tribe of Levi near, and present them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister unto him.” The Levites “shall keep his charge, and the charge of the whole congregation”, and “thou shalt give the Levites unto Aaron and to his sons.”

“And thou shalt appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall wait on their priest’s office: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.”

That is the order Judah kept: “the priests, which minister unto the Lord, are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites wait upon their business.” “for we keep the charge of the Lord our God; but ye have forsaken him.” Jeroboam made priests of whoever would consecrate himself, the very strangers the law said must not come nigh.

precepts.text: The tribe of Levi is given to Aaron and his sons to keep the charge and do the service of the tabernacle.
precepts.point: The priests were set in their divisions and the Levites in their courses as it is written in the book of Moses, every man having his ordered task.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

precepts.why:
At the dedication “they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God, which is at Jerusalem; as it is written in the book of Moses.” The book of Moses is Numbers 3: “Bring the tribe of Levi near, and present them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister unto him.”

The Levites “shall keep his charge, and the charge of the whole congregation before the tabernacle of the congregation, to do the service of the tabernacle”, and “they shall keep all the instruments of the tabernacle of the congregation, and the charge of the children of Israel.” The Lord gave the Levites to Aaron and his sons: “they are wholly given unto him out of the children of Israel.”

So when the house was finished and the children of the captivity kept the dedication with joy, offering the hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs and twelve he goats for a sin offering for all Israel, it was a great praise, and the Levites' hands were full doing the service. Every man had his ordered task, the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their courses, just as Moses wrote.
